=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1729-1730 (integration_value) and 1773-1776 (main loop) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: integration_value returns "" (not None) for empty-backtick values on Integration branch lines, e.g. rest = " \`" after label stripping. The main loop at 1773 checks `if value is not None`, so "" is accepted as a match and the parser exits before checking Target branch labels.
  WHY: For issue bodies like `"Integration branch: \`\nTarget branch: \`real/branch\`\n"` (BODIES line 50) and `"Integration branch:   \nTarget branch: \`real/branch\`\n"` (BODIES line 51), the helper returns "" (no branch) while `extract_integration_branch` returns "real/branch". The parity test `test_shell_parser_matches_python_parser` compares `_shell_parse(body)` against `extract_integration_branch(body)` and would fail for both entries. The callers (`close_merged_issues_sweep` and `issue_pr_status.yml`) would treat such issues as having no integration branch, disqualifying them from non-default-branch merge closure when they should qualify.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1770-1772 (comment) | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment claims "extract_integration_branch returns it as """ for empty/whitespace-only Integration branch values, but `extract_integration_branch` uses `re.search(body)` with `re.MULTILINE`.
  WHY: When the Integration branch line has an empty value, the regex does not match that line (group requires 1+ chars), so `re.search` continues to subsequent lines. For bodies where a valid Target branch follows, `extract_integration_branch` returns that Target branch value, not "".
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
